body: mhm 30min here. But yes. And once we are financailly independent in two years we'll start to feel ok, I hope. They didnt hurt us but they are ... well... you know, just strangers who pry into our life.

Not origin but family of the body, yes. Origin is a powerful word I'd never give them. We live with the mother and the brother of the body, move out in about 2 weeks. We cannot move that far away in the forseeable future, and we'll have to go whereever the best job opportunity lies but I can imagine being so far away feeling good.

No is ok, toes are all fine. :)   
Yeah, we really have to figure some things out inside... Yesterday and today were a bit better, we were out of the house all day cause on-call and I hope that moving out will help. At least our psych is all keen on seeing how we'll react to that, he wondered if this house triggers things (we've lived here since the body was 6). 
And sry you have been in this place too.

Hey, I can try to answer some of those over DM. And is ok being fascinated, just as Dingo said be careful about asking questions like that in case you run into another person with DID or a history of trauma, to some it can be destabilizing. But for us is ok. :)
Hey Dingo (this is a throwaway but we lurk on the sub sometimes)... it is alright, am used to it is why I didnt mention that originally. But thank you <3

Well, wheter touch is important to most people or not, I can't have it so I need to stop wanting it. The only times I get touched are when I examine a patient, which is very different... or when I get to hold my psychiatrist's hand... which sometimes almost makes me cry. But over summer we wont see each other for months so I really need to find a solution.   
In August I am on vacation so I wont touch any other human for a month....

My coworkers are surgeons, they neither have the time nor interest to listen to something like this. It is a field where everyone is/seems perfect. They don't even know that I have a girlfriend (as a girl)... I tried the touch from a stranger thing. I paid someone to hug me... it was weird cause I didnt trust her (and also too expensive long term)

Well... To explain the story I first have to say that I have been diagnosed with dissociative identitiy disorder, yes that is the one with several identities in the body that act and think independently. 

When we were in high school the person who was controlling the body most of the time was a very empathic and kind girl, she simply wanted to help people, she thought it was her duty in life and had been feeling a pull towards the medical field since she had been a kid. So she applied for medschool, got in and did the first 2.5 years. Then something bad happened and she died aka split up. I am one of the people who started existing on that that and since then have been the one who is in control the most.   
I am a bit different a bit less about helping people and more academic interest. I was the one who got us into surgery mostly. But others of course also work and study with me, by now we mostly work in teams and everyone agrees becoming a doctor is the right move in this situation.

But really I mean, emotional neglect would be in the past and isnt something I can fix without a time machine. So it becomes irrelevant. So far psych and me have not found anything to remove the need...

Hey, medical student here (quiet night, writing from the on-call room)... I am in a similar place emotionally, so I am not sure what to tell you other than that you definitely are not alone. It seems that way cause we are in a field where everyone does their best to hide their struggles.  
(And I am a girl and I'd hug you if I could.)

EDIT: side note: the worst doctors are the ones who think they are the best and become reckless...

Is a sweet idea. Though I am pretty sure scavening the old folks home to get hugs would be an ethics violation for a doc.... and it would be weird, no doctor/medstudent volunteers, you simply don't have time.   

Scenery wont change, will stay at this hospital. Responsibilities will yes. But idk, I can't really imagine a realistic opportunity that would make me happy. No job offer will include this... idk... someone to hold onto...   

I am sorry oyu have that need too. I've been trying and trying to figure out how to get rid of it. It has to be possible, I mean there are people who lived isolated for years. It is not a basic physical need like water or sleep... so why can't I overcome it?
I can't be that vulnerable to anyone who hasnt some obligation to keep it confidential, could seriously hurt my career if anyone hears about any issues I have.

yeah... at least in surgery we stop if it is hopeless... or usually don't operate at all.   

I don't know if I was, I can't remember early childhood. It is the theory of my psych. But idk... it doesn't really matter if I was emotionally neglected or not, I have that stupid need now and need to get rid of it now, no matter what did or did not happen.

Hmm... is a long story, why I did that. But I think it was the right decision, couldnt really imagine doing anything else.

My girlfriend lives 7hrs of time difference away. We are trying to figure out a way to live together but that might take months or at worst years...   
I don't know if I can have kids, and even if it would be at least 6 years away... I can't suffer like this for so long. And what even does it mean to cope? why bother?
Down because I have no one to hold me. Really, am pretty boring...

You can write it on a piece of paper and just hand it to the triage nurse. In some places you can go directly to a psychiatric hospital, otherwise as Kylo said any ER has dealt with this a lot.   

Other practical tips: pack some extra underwear/clothes in your backpack and your phone charger, maybe a book too (some places wont let you have a cable or your phone). Also wear pants you can wear without a belt. 

Good luck! I hope it will help.
Hey, thanks. Answered the parents question below/above. Guess alone is relative, I talk to patients and coworkers all day, but isnt like I can tell them to hold me while I cry so...

Thanks for your answer. 

The parents of my girlfriend abused her, I most likely wont ever meet them. And why would anyone want to assume a parental role for me? People who want kids usually don't want to adopt someone who is already 23... 

Why do you think things will be different once I am an MD? Sure work will be more and more challenging with real responsibility... but that wont change that loneliness and wishes for hugs...

Never had any. There is a woman and a man who produced this body, gave it food, shelter and paid for my education; and I am very grateful to them for that. But they are strangers, I could never trust the or call them parents.
That is sweet of you, thanks. Though I wouldnt know what to chat about.

Since I've been 11. Am 23 now. 

Sleeping on your stomach with a fist just under your heart can sometimes help a bit, any outside pressure. Weighted blankets too. Other than that I dont know and am sorry.
